Yes: the matching paper is On the Computational Complexity of Structural Generalization by Zichao Wei [1]. It argues that structural generalization can be formally defined from compositional structure and unbounded generalization, and frames the key complexity result as a gap between an NC^1 lower bound and the learnable ceiling TC^0 of pure Transformers [1]. Under its Montagovian setup, semantic tree evaluation is an NC^1-complete instance, so under the standard assumption TC^0 ≠ NC^1, a pure Transformer cannot learn structural generalization [1].

A related Wei paper is more empirical: Structural Generalization on SLOG without Hand-Written Rules presents a neural cellular automaton with a discrete bottleneck that learns compositional rules from data and achieves strong structural generalization on SLOG without hand-written rules [2]. So [1] is the complexity/theory paper, while [2] studies a learned alternative and analyzes its success and failure patterns on a benchmark [2].
